Lessons.Title: How Many Do You See? PLC Activity
ExplanationParagraphs:
Learning goal: You will apply your understanding of equal groups and multiplication to create a How Many Do You See activity.
This lesson provides an opportunity to observe the ways in which you find the number of objects in equal groups. After the warm-up, you create your own How Many Do You See activity and then facilitate it with other you in the class.

Warm-up How Many Do You See: Equal Groups (10 minutes). Discuss how a group of dots may be perceived through different equal-group arrangements. The original displayed source dot image's pixel geometry has not been verified.

Activity 1 Design Your How Many Do You See (20 minutes): draw a dot image that can be perceived in equal groups, and list different ways classmates might count it. Preserve student-created dot geometry.

Activity 2 Facilitate Your How Many Do You See (15 minutes): flash the dot image, ask how many learners see and how they see them, allow 30 seconds of silent thinking, display again, hold a one-minute peer discussion and record different group strategies.
Independent example: a 3 × 4 dot array has 12 dots. Learners might see three rows of four or four columns of three; both total 12 with different grouping language.
The original publisher reflection Cool-down is gated. Teacher checks original student art, counting, reasoning and facilitation rather than awarding automatic credit for a single number.
Source-authentic activity scripts are teacher mediated. Figures, print-only masters and publisher-gated Cool-downs not independently inspected are not claimed source-identical.

KeyConcepts.Title: Preserved valid source-bound concepts
KeyConcepts.Definition:
Key ideas:
- Apply understanding of equal groups and multiplication to create a How Many Do You See activity
- This lesson provides an opportunity to observe the ways in which you find the number of objects in equal groups
- Compare actual values or measured attributes, not the visual size or position of a drawing.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Use in conjunction with the individually verified 2021 activity directions.
KeyConcepts.Example: Learning goal: You will apply your understanding of equal groups and multiplication to create a How Many Do You See activity.

KeyConcepts.Title: Structured subitizing
KeyConcepts.Definition: Recognize a total by seeing manageable groups rather than counting every dot.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Explain how groups compose the whole.
KeyConcepts.Example: Three groups of four dots make 12.

KeyConcepts.Title: Equivalent arrays
KeyConcepts.Definition: Reorganize a total into different equal-group views.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Products may be equal even when the interpreted orientation changes.

KeyConcepts.Title: Facilitated dot talk
KeyConcepts.Definition: Briefly show, hide, redisplay and discuss an authored image.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Record multiple valid observations with group and total counts.
KeyConcepts.Example: 30 seconds silent view, then one minute pair dialogue.

WorkedExamples.Title: Independent dot arrangement
WorkedExamples.Question: A first-party 3-row-by-4-column arrangement: find two group interpretations.
WorkedExamples.Check: Explain the mathematical relationship, and keep independently authored examples distinct from source worksheets.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Counting a different total for each correct grouping interpretation.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Regrouping equal groups should not change the total.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Assuming only one perspective is mathematically allowed.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: An array admits row and column views.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Record and explain multiple valid perspectives.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Claiming a created dot layout copies the uninspected source figure.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Source pixels have not been independently checked.
